Sommerjobb for ungdom og unge voksne i kommunal sektor
description: KS ønsker tilbud på et FoU-prosjekt som kan gi en nasjonal oversikt over omfang og bruk av sommervikarer i kommunal sektor. I tillegg skal det utvikles tips og råd som gir struktur og plan for helhetlig arbeidet med sommerjobb gjennom hele året, og som kan sees i forhold til HR-systemer kommuner og fylkeskommuner benytter. KS har behov for en samlet oversikt og innsikt i omfang og organisering av sommerjobb for ungdom og unge voksne. KS har behov for systematisert kunnskap om hvilke grep som fungerer, hvilke barrierer som finnes, og hvordan sommerjobbene oppleves av ungdommene og unge voksne selv. Et slikt kunnskapsgrunnlag er nødvendig for å kunne støtte kommuner og fylkeskommuner for å vurdere hvordan sommerjobber og andre småjobber kan bidra til økt rekruttering, inkludering og attraktivitet i kommunal sektor. På grunnlag av kunnskapsinnhentingen skal det utvikles tips og råd, som gir struktur og plan for helhetlig arbeid med sommerjobber gjennom hele året, som kan sees i forhold til kommunale og fylkeskommunale HR-systemer og som enkelt kan tas i bruk av arbeidsgiverne i kommunal sektor.

title: Netherlands – Research consultancy services – Monitor Prenatale Screening - Niet Invasieve Prenatale test (NIPT) en het structureel echoscopisch onderzoek (SEO)
description: Als onderdeel van de regietaak is het RIVM verantwoordelijk voor monitoring en evaluatie van de prenatale screening. Het gaat hierbij om de Niet-Invasieve Prenatale Test (NIPT) en het Structureel Echoscopisch Onderzoek (SEO), inclusief voorafgaande counseling. In dat kader worden jaarlijks twee landelijke monitors (plus een Engelse vertaling) opgesteld om de kwaliteit en bereikbaarheid van deze screening te bewaken, knelpunten (in de zorgketen) te signaleren, bij te kunnen sturen, maar ook om te verantwoorden naar de opdrachtgever VWS en de ketenpartners. De werkzaamheden met de huidige leverancier lopen 31 december 2026 af. Een nieuwe overeenkomst voor de monitoring van PNS moet door aanbestedende dienst worden aanbesteed. Scope van de opdracht De opdracht betreft het uitvoeren van de jaarlijkse landelijke monitoring van NIPT-SEO aan de hand van vastgestelde indicatoren. Deze bestaat uit: 1. een monitor geaggregeerd op landelijk niveau in het Nederlands en Engels; 2. een gedetailleerdere professionalsmonitor geaggregeerd op regionaal niveau in het Nederlands. Producten uit voorgaande jaren zijn terug te vinden op Monitor | Prenatale en neonatale screeningen (www.pns.nl). Daarin is ook te zien dat de VWS-monitor de trend op hoofdlijnen in de afgelopen jaren toont. De professionalsmonitor gaat ook in op regionale verschillen. Hierin er worden ook trends gepresenteerd op landelijk niveau. Looptijd van de overeenkomst Het doel van deze Europese aanbesteding is het afsluiten van een dienstverleningsovereenkomst met één opdrachtnemer voor de monitoring van PNS. De beoogde ingangsdatum van de af te sluiten overeenkomst is 1 januari 2027. De aanbestedende dienst wenst een overeenkomst met de opdrachtnemer te sluiten voor een initiële periode van vier (4) jaar, met aanvullend drie (3) maal een optie tot verlenging van één (1) jaar. Dit resulteert in een maximale looptijd van de overeenkomst van zeven (7) jaar.

title: Finland – Clothing, footwear, luggage articles and accessories – Pysäköinninvalvonnan virkapuvun hankinta
description: Helsingin kaupungin pysäköinninvalvonta pyytää tarjouksia pysäköinnintarkastajien virkapuvuista. Tällä tarjouspyynnöllä pyydetään tarjouksia n. 80 pysäköinnintarkastajan ammattikäyttöön tarkoitetuista virkapuvuista. Virkapuvun on täytettävä tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä asetetut vaatimukset, virkapukua koskeva lainsäädäntö. Pysäköinnintarkastajat työskentelevät ulkotiloissa kaikkina vuodenaikoina, joten virkapuvun on sovelluttava kaikille mahdollisille sääolosuhteille, esimerkiksi vesi- ja lumisateelle sekä paahtavaan auringonpaisteeseen. Pysäköinnintarkastajien virkapukuun sisältyvät vaatteet ja tarkempi kuvaus niiden ominaisuuksista löytyy tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä. Tarjouskilpailussa valitaan yksi sopimuskumppani. Sopimuksen arvioitu alkamisajankohta on syksyllä 2026, ja ensimmäisen erän toimitus on suunniteltu tehtäväksi talvikaudelle 2026-2027. Sopimus tehdään 5 vuoden määräaikaisena, jonka jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Pitkäkestoisella sopimuksella pyritään takaamaan pysäköinnintarkastajien käyttämien vaatteiden malliston pysyvyys ja yhtenäisyys. Tarjouskilpailuun osallistuvien yritysten tulee toimittaa hankintayksikölle materiaalinäytteet sekä mallikappaleet osasta tarjottavista vaatteista, jotta hankintayksikkö voi arvioida tarjottavien vaatteiden vaatimusten täyttymisen ja suorittaa laatuvertailun. Toimitusten sisältö ja aikataulu on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnöllä ja liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.

Keravan kaupunki omistaa ja hallinnoi laajaa kiinteistökantaa, johon kuuluu muun muassa: - kouluja - päiväkoteja - liikuntapaikkoja - toimistorakennuksia - muita kaupungin käytössä olevia rakennuksia. Kiinteistöjen hallinta edellyttää useiden eri tietojen ja prosessien yhteensovittamista, kuten: - kunnossapito ja huoltotehtävät - energiankulutus - vedenkulutus - olosuhdetiedot - hälytykset ja poikkeamat - raportointi ja analytiikka. Nykyisessä toimintaympäristössä näitä tietoja hallitaan useissa eri järjestelmissä sekä osittain manuaalisissa prosesseissa. Tiedon hajautuminen vaikeuttaa kokonaiskuvan muodostamista kiinteistöjen tilasta ja hidastaa päätöksentekoa. Lisäksi kiinteistöjen ylläpidossa korostuu yhä enemmän tarve: - parantaa energiatehokkuutta - tunnistaa poikkeamat nopeasti - siirtyä ennakoivaan kunnossapitoon - hyödyntää dataa päätöksenteon tukena. Tämän vuoksi Keravan kaupunki hankkii keskitetyn järjestelmän, joka yhdistää kiinteistöihin liittyvän operatiivisen ja analysoitavan tiedon yhteen palveluun.

title: Netherlands – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Sputtering Tool
description: Scope of the Contract The scope of this Contract for the Sputtering tool includes the following: For the execution of high-level scientific research within the Zernike Institute for Advanced Materials, the availability of an advanced sputter deposition system is essential. This equipment enables the fabrication of high-quality thin films from a wide range of materials, including metals, alloys and insulating materials. Such thin films are essential for a broad range of research activities in the fields of nanotechnology, materials science and functional systems. The intended sputtering system will be integrated into the existing facilities of the Zernike Nanolab and must be suitable for use within a shared academic research environment. The system will be used for both routine deposition processes and advanced experiments requiring a high degree of process stability, reproducibility and material purity. This will enable the development and characterization of new material combinations, multilayers and structures, thereby contributing to the scientific output and research ambitions of the institute. In addition, the sputtering system will play an important role in the education and training of PhD candidates and students. Access to modern deposition equipment enables users to gain practical experience with thin-film technology and vacuum processes, thereby supporting the development of technical and scientific expertise within the organization. A minimum warranty period of three (3) years is included, covering defects in materials, workmanship and installation, including parts and labour, as well as timely remote and on-site technical support in the event of equipment malfunction. A service contract for at least three (3) years is included, covering preventive maintenance, calibration, software updates and technical support. User and technical staff training for safe and effective operation and basic maintenance of the system is included.

title: Denmark – Hotel services – 16.06 Hotelophold (2027)
description: SKI udbyder en rammeaftale vedrørende indkøb af hotelophold i Danmark samt i Grønland og på Færøerne, benævnt 16.06 Hotelophold (2027) Rammeaftalen udbydes som én samlet aftale med geografisk dækning i Danmark samt i Grønland og på Færøerne, hvor der på forhånd reserveres et antal pladser til hoteller i specifikke afgrænsede geografiske områder, som er inddelt i områder og distrikter for at sikre en bred dækning af hoteller, der kan imødekomme SKI’s kunders indkøbsbehov. Det er således målet at få et bredt udsnit af hoteller fordelt i hele Danmark og i afgrænsede områder i Grønland og på Færøerne. Rammeaftalen indgås mellem SKI og leverandøren. Da der tildeles flere leverandører, indgås der i praksis en række parallelle rammeaftaler i mellem SKI og leverandørerne, én for hver tildelt leverandør. De parallelle rammeaftaler er enslydende. SKI's kunder er oprindelige parter på rammeaftalen og de parallelle rammeaftaler, og kan dermed anvende disse og overholder deres udbudspligt. Rammeaftalen forventes at blive tildelt 267 hoteller. Processen er nærmere beskrevet i udbudsbetingelserne punkt 8.3.1. Kundernes tildeling af leveringskontrakter sker i henhold til Bilag D Brug af Rammeaftalen. Staten som helhed er forpligtet til at anvende rammeaftalen. Det fremgår af bilag A og A.1 hvilke kunder som kan anvende Rammeaftalen.

description: Pohjois-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue (Pohde) pyytää omasta ja siihen kuuluvan yhteistyöalueen yksiköiden puolesta tarjoustanne apteekin steriileistä elatusaineista. Hankinnan kohteena ovat apteekin steriilit mikrobiologiset elatusaineet, joita käytetään puhdastilaympäristössä steriilien lääkevalmisteiden valmistusprosessien kontrollointiin sekä aseptisten työmenetelmien testaukseen. Sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella yhden vuoden mittaisella optiokaudella. Tarjouspyynnössä ilmoitetut hankintamäärät ovat arvioituja yhden vuoden kulutusmääriä ja ne ilmoitetaan tarjoajille ainoastaan tarjouksen tekemisen tueksi. title: Finland – Software package and information systems – Työkykyjohtamisen järjestelmän hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on työkykyjohtamisen järjestelmä SaaS-palveluna. Hankintaan sisältyvät järjestelmän toimitus, käyttöönoton suunnittelu ja toteutus, tarvittavien integraatioiden toteuttaminen sekä jatkuvat ylläpito- ja tukipalvelut. Lisäksi tilaajalla on mahdollisuus hankkia erikseen sovittavaa pienkehitystä sopimuskauden aikana. Toimittaja vastaa siitä, että järjestelmä voidaan ottaa käyttöön hallitusti ja että se integroidaan tilaajan keskeisiin taustajärjestelmiin, kuten henkilöstö- ja identiteetinhallintajärjestelmiin. Vanhojen tietojen siirto voidaan toteuttaa asiantuntijatyönä hintaliitteessä ilmoitetun asiantuntijatyön tuntihinnan mukaisesti erikseen tilattavana optiona. Tilaaja päättää option käyttöönotosta oman harkintansa mukaan sopimuskauden aikana, eikä tilaajalla ole velvollisuutta ottaa optiota käyttöön tai tilata siihen liittyviä palveluita. Järjestelmän tulee tukea tilaajan työkykyjohtamisen toimintamalleja ja prosesseja, erityisesti varhaisen tuen käytäntöjä, sairauspoissaolojen hallintaa, työkykyriskien tunnistamista ja ennaltaehkäisyä sekä työhön paluun tukemista. Ratkaisun tavoitteena on parantaa työkykytoimenpiteiden oikea-aikaisuutta, lisätä toiminnan läpinäkyvyyttä sekä vahvistaa tiedolla johtamista organisaation kaikilla tasoilla. Järjestelmän tulee tarjota ajantasainen kokonaiskuva työkykytilanteesta työntekijä-, yksikkö- ja organisaatiotasolla. Sen on muodostettava selkeä, käyttäjäystävällinen ja intuitiivinen kokonaisuus työkykyjohtamisen prosesseista sekä tarjottava käyttäjäroolien mukaiset näkymät ja käyttöoikeudet. Käyttäjäryhmiä ovat vähintään esihenkilöt, HR:n työkykyasiantuntijat, johto sekä järjestelmän pääkäyttäjät. Esihenkilöiden tulee voida hyödyntää järjestelmää päivittäisessä työkykyjohtamisen työssä, kun taas johdolle järjestelmän tulee tarjota koontinäkymiä, raportointia ja analytiikkaa strategisen päätöksenteon tueksi. Järjestelmän tulee mahdollistaa monipuolinen raportointi eri aikajaksoille ja organisaatiotasoille sekä tarjota visuaalisia näkymiä, kuten kehityssuuntia, vertailuja ja tunnuslukuja päätöksenteon tueksi. Toimittajan tulee toteuttaa käyttöönotto yhteistyössä tilaajan kanssa siten, että ratkaisu vastaa tilaajan toiminnallisia tarpeita ja käyttöönotto tukee sujuvaa siirtymistä tuotantokäyttöön. Hankinnan tavoitteena on parantaa työkykyjohtamisen vaikuttavuutta, vähentää sairauspoissaoloista aiheutuvia kustannuksia, vahvistaa ennakoivaa johtamista sekä tukea henkilöstön työkykyä, työssä suoriutumista ja työssä jatkamista. Järjestelmän tulee olla moderni, tietoturvallinen, skaalautuva ja helppokäyttöinen ratkaisu, joka tukee tilaajan toiminnan pitkäjänteistä kehittämistä.

Ateriat kuljetetaan pääsääntöisesti aamupäivisin koulujen ja päiväkotien aukioloaikoina. Reittiliitteessä on määritelty kuljetusaikataulut sekä ajoreitit. Noormarkunyhtenäiskoulun keittiön osalta tarjouspyynnössä on mukana reittien 1-2 viennit ja noudot tarjouspyynnön mukaisesti. title: Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) Multi Domain Task Force (MDTF) Buildings (BLDGs) 3218 and 3219
description: SOLICITATION NUMBER: W912DW26RA014 TITLE: Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) Multi Domain Task Force (MDTF) Buildings (BLDGs) 3218 and 3219 LOCATION: JBLM, Washington FSC CODE: Y1AZ - Construction of Other Administrative Facilities and Service Buildings NAICS CODE: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ISSUE DATE: On or about 29 January 2026 RESPONSE DATE: On or about early-mid March 2026 100% Small Business Set-Aside Construction of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) Multi Domain Task Force(MDTF) Buildings (BLDGs) 3218 and 3219. FOR INFORMATION ONLY: This Synopsis is ONLY A NOTIFICATION that a solicitation is anticipated and forthcoming. All questions regarding this SYNOPSIS should be submitted in writing via email to the Contract Specialist as noted below. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Seattle District anticipates solicitation and award of a Firm-Fixed Price contract resulting from Request for Proposal (RFP) W912DW26RA014. The project intends to convert two (2) existing barrack buildings into operational facilities for 3 tier levels of command located at JBLM. This RFP is available to all business firms with active SAM registration under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 236.204(ii), construction magnitude is estimated to be in the range of $25,000,000 to $100,000,000. 100 percent payment and performance bonds will be required. The project intends to will convert two (2) existing barrack buildings into operational facilities for 3 tier levels of command. These buildings in general are referred as �the Hammer Heads�. title: Notice of Intent for the Department of Transportation (DOT) to Implement Executive Order 14398 � Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors
description: Notice of Intent for the Department of Transportation (DOT) to Implement Executive Order 14398 � Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL Consistent with Administration priorities and applicable law, the Department of Transportation (DOT) hereby provides notice of its intent to take immediate action to implement Executive Order (E.O.) 14398, Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors (March 26, 2026). E.O. 14398 establishes that Federal agencies shall not do business with contractors that engage in racially discriminatory diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) activities. On April 20, 2026, the Federal Acquisition Regulatory (FAR) Council issued model deviation text to implement E.O. 14398, directing agencies to update their Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) class deviations for FAR Parts 9, 12, 22, and 52. In alignment with this direction, DOT issued FAR Class Deviation 2026-24 on April 24, 2026, implementing the required changes pending formal FAR rulemaking. Effective immediately, Contracting Officers shall insert the required E.O. 14398 clause in all new solicitations and resulting contracts valued above the micro-purchase threshold, including those for commercial products and commercial services, where the place of delivery or performance is in the United States. DOT is concurrently updating its existing contract portfolio to incorporate the requirements of E.O. 14398. Contracting Officers shall make every effort to bilaterally modify existing contracts no later than July 24, 2026. DOT is implementing E.O. 14398 as a matter of policy and compliance. Contractors seeking to compete for, or continue performing, DOT contracts should ensure alignment with E.O. 14398 and associated requirements.

title: Bitterroot Front 10 Year G-Z IRSC
description: 10/29/2025: Added mapbooks for mandatory and optional contract areas 10/16/2025: Share draft documents and information on second site visit 7/17/2025: Added Industry meeting attendees, presentation and notes The U.S. Forest Service is re-issuing this formal Request for Information (RFI) in connection with the Bitterroot National Forest 10-Year Integrated Resource Stewardship Contract IRSC for projects in the Bitterroot Front Landscape Planning Area and potentially other areas across the forest. The objectives of this initiative are to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire by accelerating and expanding forest restoration treatments and to bolster the region�s wood utilization capacity by providing a consistent supply of wood products. Project Overview and Scope: Approximately 13,000 acres is planned for treatment across the Bitterroot Front Planning Area over a 10?year period, with the potential to add more acres adjacent to the planning area. Four project areas may be offered at contract award for immediate implementation. Additional project areas are planned to be offered on an annual basis subject to funding. Two project areas may be offered for timber sale layout at the start of this project. A minimum of 90,000 CCF (approximately 45 million board feet) of commercial timber is anticipated to be offered over the contract life; volumes may fluctuate annually. Types of Service Work contemplated include: Road maintenance, reconditioning, construction, and decommissioning. Reconstruction plans and design are not contemplated to be activities. Timber removal including logging and transportation. Timber sale preparation activities which include harvest unit layout, GPS traversing, unit boundary marking, interior marking and cruising. Biomass removal including thinning non-merchantable material, slashing, chipping, staging, transportation and other related activities. Anticipated Terms: Minimum timber value estimates will be based on base rates and/or appraised rates if appropriate as determined from the Forest Service�s Timber appraisal system.?Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive pricing on offered forest products at the task order level as projects are issued. Payment terms for service work items are anticipated to be by the acre or linear foot for most treatments. Road maintenance and reconstruction activities may be priced by the mile or contract quantity. If transportation of forest products is a service item, delivered tons or CCF are anticipated to be used. Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive prices at the task order level as projects are solicited. The projects may include both mandatory and optional service items; product value at awarded rates will be used to offset the cost-of-service work items. Davis-Bacon wages and certified payrolls will be required for all Road Construction requirements. Service Contract Act wages will apply towards all non-construction service work requirements. Road construction requirements will be subject to bonding at applicable regulatory thresholds. Depending on the scale of scope in task orders, 3-5 year periods of performance are contemplated. A site visit is scheduled for October 28, 2025, to discuss the project in detail and share information. There is no planned virtual option for this site visit at this time. Additionally, draft documents are being shared. These materials are being provided for information and review purposes only. This is NOT a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. This request does not obligate the Government in any contract award. Feedback, comments, or questions regarding the draft documents are welcome and may be submitted to the contact person listed below.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: ****Updated 18 MAR 2020, Due to the COVID-19 spread and site closure the Technical Read Library Access is currently suspended until at least 11 MAY 2020. Please note that depending on the state of things this date can be pushed out further or rescined earlier.**** ****Updated 13 FEB 2020, Posted an Updated version of the Industry Day Attendees List**** ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. The solicitation and any amendments thereto will only be available by downloading the documents from the website. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring the site for the release of amendments (if any) or other information pertaining to the solicitation. It is anticipated that the website will provide a registration service that will send an e-mail notification when a change is made to the solicitation. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Bernard J. Clarke AFRL/RIGD 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2106 Email: Bernard.Clarke@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below: Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. PLEASE SEE THE ATTACHED GEOPEX SYNOPSIS v12.doc AMENDMENT 1 to BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 The purpose of this amendment to BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 is to update the mailing instructions in Section IV.3.c to remove the requirement for a hard copy to be mailed. The updated mailing instructions are below: Part II, Section IV.3.c. is updated as follows: c. MAILING INSTRUCTIONS. Email Unclassified electronic submission to the TPOC identified in Section VII. Encrypt or password-protect all proprietary information prior to sending. Offerors are responsible to confirm receipt with the TPOC. AFRL is not responsible for undelivered documents. If electronic submission is used, only one copy of the documentation is required. Questions can be directed to the TPOC listed in Section VII. No other changes are made. Amendment No. 2 to BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 The purpose of this amendment is to: Section III, Eligibility Information, adds the following paragraph 5 for S&T Protection: 5. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Contractors/Recipients are required to submit with their proposal a Standard Form 424, "Research and Related and Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded), as well as a Security Program Questionnaire, which are included in the RI-Specific Proposal Preparation Instructions and can be accessed at: https://sam.gov/opp/e628c811fafe041accdddf55fb8539bf/view?keywords=AFRL-BAA-GUIDE&sort=-relevance&index=&is_active=true&page=1. Always reference the newest versions of these documents. Complete and submit the required forms with your proposal to the technical point of contact (TPOC) listed in Section VII-Agency Contacts AND AFRL.RIOF@us.af.mil. Contractors will be required to provide documentation of their Security Program Plan for initial Institution S&T Protection Program Review. The purpose of requesting the plan is to evaluate the offeror�s capacity for protecting the Government�s S&T and failure to demonstrate a plan adequate to meet the needs of the requirement may be grounds for considering the proposal unawardable. In the event a security risk is identified and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Contractor/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will be only required to provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. After award, the Contractor/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Standard Form 424 as an annual requirement to the points of contact listed above. No other changes are made. title: Trash, Debris, and Metal Removal
description: This is a presolicitation notice for a competitive solicitation that GPO intends to post on or about July 17th, 2026. The scope of work includes: The United States Government Publishing Office (GPO) is constantly under renovation due to office moves, production improvements, infrastructure modifications, and facility maintenance. As a result, GPO requires on-call and scheduled removal of non-hazardous debris, recyclable scrap metal, and paper dust. GPO�s Plant Operations Division requires two (2) 40-yard roll-off dumpsters and one (1) 30-yard recyclable metal roll-off dumpster. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, roll-off dumpsters, transportation, permits, and disposal services necessary to provide on-call removal, transportation, recycling, and disposal of non-hazardous debris, and recyclable scrap metal generated by GPO. The United States Government Publishing Office has 3 shifts in the building, and it is imperative that the trash be removed for the health and safety for all the employees at GPO. As a result, GPO requires the trash compacter be exchanged every Tuesday and Friday. This statement of work covers the trash compacter exchange for the trash collected for GPO�s Building A, B, C and D. A site visit will be scheduled for Tuesday, July 28th, 2026 10:30-11:30AM EST.

description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) Pacific Region, Guam requires reliable commercial cellular telephone services, including voice, text, data, and international roaming capabilities, to support official Government operations for DeCA Guam. The objective of this requirement is to procure cellular service plans and necessary equipment for five (5) key personnel (3 Store lines and 2 CDC lines). The Contractor shall provide commercial cellular services, equipment (Bring Your Own Device(BYOD) compatibility or carrier-provided devices), and comprehensive coverage for five (5) lines. The requirement includes a Base Year and four (4) 12-month Option Years. Each of the five (5) lines must include an unlimited tier commercial service planfeaturing Unlimited domestic Voice and SMS text messaging, Unlimited high-speed mobile data, Unlimited mobile hotspot data sharing capabilities, U.S. calls included at no additional roaming/long-distance charge. Personnel require reliable connectivity while traveling on official business throughout the Pacific region and the continental United States and Service must include up to thirty (30) days per year, per line, of unlimited roaming coverage to United States (CONUS/OCONUS), Japan, SouthKorea and Germany.

description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. title: Bitterroot Front 10 Year G-Z IRSC
description: 10/16/2025: Share draft documents and information on second site visit 7/17/2025: Added Industry meeting attendees, presentation and notes The U.S. Forest Service is re-issuing this formal Request for Information (RFI) in connection with the Bitterroot National Forest 10-Year Integrated Resource Stewardship Contract IRSC for projects in the Bitterroot Front Landscape Planning Area and potentially other areas across the forest. The objectives of this initiative are to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire by accelerating and expanding forest restoration treatments and to bolster the region�s wood utilization capacity by providing a consistent supply of wood products. Project Overview and Scope: Approximately 13,000 acres is planned for treatment across the Bitterroot Front Planning Area over a 10?year period, with the potential to add more acres adjacent to the planning area. Four project areas may be offered at contract award for immediate implementation. Additional project areas are planned to be offered on an annual basis subject to funding. Two project areas may be offered for timber sale layout at the start of this project. A minimum of 90,000 CCF (approximately 45 million board feet) of commercial timber is anticipated to be offered over the contract life; volumes may fluctuate annually. Types of Service Work contemplated include: Road maintenance, reconditioning, construction, and decommissioning. Reconstruction plans and design are not contemplated to be activities. Timber removal including logging and transportation. Timber sale preparation activities which include harvest unit layout, GPS traversing, unit boundary marking, interior marking and cruising. Biomass removal including thinning non-merchantable material, slashing, chipping, staging, transportation and other related activities. Anticipated Terms: Minimum timber value estimates will be based on base rates and/or appraised rates if appropriate as determined from the Forest Service�s Timber appraisal system.?Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive pricing on offered forest products at the task order level as projects are issued. Payment terms for service work items are anticipated to be by the acre or linear foot for most treatments. Road maintenance and reconstruction activities may be priced by the mile or contract quantity. If transportation of forest products is a service item, delivered tons or CCF are anticipated to be used. Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive prices at the task order level as projects are solicited. The projects may include both mandatory and optional service items; product value at awarded rates will be used to offset the cost-of-service work items. Davis-Bacon wages and certified payrolls will be required for all Road Construction requirements. Service Contract Act wages will apply towards all non-construction service work requirements. Road construction requirements will be subject to bonding at applicable regulatory thresholds. Depending on the scale of scope in task orders, 3-5 year periods of performance are contemplated. A site visit is scheduled for October 28, 2025, to discuss the project in detail and share information. There is no planned virtual option for this site visit at this time. Additionally, draft documents are being shared. These materials are being provided for information and review purposes only. This is NOT a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. This request does not obligate the Government in any contract award. title: JUSTIFICATION FOR AN EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY (JEFO) Asteres Add-On to Existing Systems Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital
description: The action submitted for approval is for the acquisition of two (2) Asteres ScriptCenters for the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Military Treatment Facility (MTF): two (2) Asteres ScriptCenter located at Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital at Lackland Air Force Base (AFB). In support of this acquisition, an order will be placed under Lovell Government Services Patient Monitoring and Capital Equipment (PMCE) Contract SPE2D1-24-D-0007, valid through March 13, 2034. Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital currently has two (2) Asteres ScriptCenter in use, this procurement is for an additional Asteres ScriptCenter which will expand the available storage on site. The use of this authority is necessary for the purpose of purchasing equipment for both Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital at Lackland AFB. This add-on will expand the current Asteres ScriptCenter from two (2) to four (4) total units at the Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital at Lackland AFB. The use of this authority is necessary because Wilford Hall Ambulatory Care Hospital at Lackland AFB has set the following minimum requirements: Interoperable with the current pharmacy workflow, namely, iA NEXiA, Parata P2000, and ScriptPro SPCentral Utilizes fingerprint scanning and camera identification Able to scan the Department of Defense ID Card and match the patient to the prescriptions Must have an Authorization to Operate (ATO) on the Medical Country of Origin Information (MEDCOI) system ScriptCenter is connected using �Campus Mode,� allowing communications between systems regarding prescription locations, patient identities, and integrations with workflow and MHS Genesis. Campus Mode is a proprietary interface, developed solely by Asteres, without which an additional external will call machine would not be interoperable with Lackland PX�s current system. Asteres is the sole provider of the software subscription and maintenance support required to operate and maintain a ScriptCenter system. Further, Asteres has not entered into any agreements with other companies to resell their products or services; therefore, third party offerings are unavailable. Asteres Inc. has an Authority to Operate (ATO) on the MEDCOI network and has active interfaces with all three DHA pharmacy workflow systems (iA�s NEXiA, ScriptPro�s SP Central, and Parata�s P2000).

title: Turnkey Event Management and Production Services for the American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice only. The solicitation is not available at this time. Quotations submitted in response to this notice will not be accepted. The U.S. Department of State, U.S. Embassy Singapore, intends to issue a Request for Quotations for turnkey event planning, production, and management services for the inaugural American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival. The public festival is tentatively planned for November 2026 at Jewel Changi Airport, Level 4. The event will be designed to accommodate an anticipated attendance of at least 1,000 people. It is expected to include multiple activity zones, American corporate partners, exhibitors, entertainment, food and beverage activations, and interactive experiences highlighting American Thanksgiving, American culture, and American food ingredients and products. Scope of Requirement The contractor will serve as the single point of responsibility for the successful planning, coordination, production, execution, and closeout of the festival. The contractor will furnish all personnel, supervision, project management, equipment, materials, supplies, transportation, production services, subcontractors, vendor coordination, licenses, permits, approvals, and other resources necessary to deliver a complete and fully operational event, except for any property, services, facilities, or information expressly identified in the solicitation as Government-furnished. Required services are anticipated to include, but are not limited to: Event concept development, design, and planning Venue and stakeholder coordination Project and production management Staging, audiovisual, lighting, sound, and technical production services Event logistics, setup, teardown, and waste removal Exhibitor, sponsor, vendor, and subcontractor coordination Entertainment and programming coordination Food and beverage activation coordination Marketing and promotional support Registration, attendance, and guest-flow management Health, safety, security, and emergency planning On-site event operations and staffing Required licenses, permits, registrations, and approvals Post-event closeout and reporting On-Site Management and Subcontractor Control The prime contractor must provide active, on-the-ground management in Singapore and retain overall responsibility for all subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The prime contractor shall designate an experienced on-site event manager with authority to direct the work, control subcontractor performance, commit contractor resources, resolve operational issues, and coordinate directly with the Contracting Officer�s Representative and other event stakeholders. The on-site event manager must be available in Singapore for required planning meetings, site visits, rehearsals, setup, event execution, teardown, and closeout activities. The event manager must be continuously present at the event site during setup, rehearsals, public operating hours, and teardown. The prime contractor may subcontract portions of the work but may not delegate its overall management, supervision, quality-control, or contractual responsibilities. The prime contractor will remain fully responsible for the performance, conduct, safety, quality, and timely delivery of all work performed by its subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The solicitation will require quoters to identify their proposed on-site event manager and provide information concerning the individual�s qualifications, authority, availability, and experience managing comparable events. Quoters will also be required to describe their proposed staffing structure and approach to managing subcontractors and vendors. The final solicitation will contain the complete performance requirements, deliverables, evaluation criteria, quotation instructions, and applicable terms and conditions. Contract and Award Information The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price contract. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and make an award without discussions. Therefore, each quoter should submit its best terms in its initial quotation. Information regarding any pre-quotation conference or site visit, if applicable, will be included in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation in accordance with the solicitation, which the Government will consider. System for Award Management Registration Quoters must have an active registration in the System for Award Management at SAM.gov when submitting a quotation and at the time of contract award. SAM registration is free. Prospective quoters are encouraged to begin the registration process early because registration may take several weeks to complete. Registration assistance is available through the Federal Service Desk. Authorization to Perform in Singapore Because contract performance will take place in Singapore, the contractor must be legally authorized to operate and conduct business in Singapore. The contractor must possess all licenses, permits, registrations, approvals, and professional or technical qualifications required to perform the contract. The solicitation will include Department of State Acquisition Regulation clause 652.242-73, Authorization and Performance (AUG 1999). Under this clause, the contractor will be required to warrant that it: Has obtained authorization to operate and conduct business in Singapore Has obtained all licenses and permits necessary to perform the contract Will comply fully with all applicable Singapore laws, decrees, labor standards, and regulations throughout contract performance If a subcontractor or joint-venture partner will perform any portion of the work, that entity must also satisfy the applicable authorization, licensing, permitting, and legal-compliance requirements. The contractor will be responsible for obtaining and maintaining all required authorizations, registrations, licenses, permits, and approvals at no additional cost to the Government. The apparent successful quoter shall provide evidence of the required business authorizations, licenses, permits, registrations, and technical qualifications upon request by the Contracting Officer and before contract award. Electronic Submission Instructions for submitting quotations electronically will be included in the solicitation. Quotations submitted in response to this pre-solicitation notice will not be accepted. Other Information Prospective quoters may refer to the following Singapore Government resources: Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority: https://www.acra.gov.sg Ministry of Manpower: https://www.mom.gov.sg

title: FY26 City Pair Program Award
description: This procurement is for scheduled certificated U.S. airlines to provide passenger transportation services, Government-wide, for over 16,000 domestic/international airport or city pairs. The requirement-type contracts will be for one year beginning October 1, 2025, plus one 2-month option period and one 1-month option period. For information regarding the CRAF program, call the DOD Commercial Airlift Division at (618) 229-4801. The FY26 City Pair Program has awarded items to 7 carriers: Alaska Airlines, American Airlines, Breeze Airways, Delta Air Lines, JetBlue Airways, Southwest Airlines and United Airlines.

title: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations
description: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations As the Department�s Senior Procurement Executive, I am reaching out to share guidance due to the lapse in appropriations that occurred on October 1, 2025. This guidance relates to the handling of Department, including US Agency for International Development (USAID), contract and federal assistance (grants) awards, that is consistent with Department and Office of Management and Budget�s Guidance on Operations During a Lapse in Appropriations. The Antideficiency Act prohibits agencies from incurring obligations that are in advance of, or that exceed, an appropriation, with certain limited exceptions. As you are aware, a fiscal year 2026 appropriation is not yet enacted. For many Department accounts, this results in a lapse in funds designated to purchase certain supplies and services and issue grants and reduces the Department�s capacity to provide oversight on contracts and grants. As a result, certain planned procurements and grants may be cancelled, or postponed, and certain existing contracts and grants may be stopped, suspended, reduced in scope, or terminated. Additionally, payments may be delayed. If the lapse directly affects a contract or grant, on or about October 1, 2025, the Department�s contracting officers and grant officers will notify contractors and recipients of the status of their contract or grant. If a contract or grant will not be affected at the onset of the lapse in appropriations, the Department does not plan to provide any separate notifications or communications of that fact. Unless the contracting officer or grants officer provides a formal notification to the contrary, all Department contractors and recipients must continue to comply with all terms, conditions, requirements and deliveries specified in their contracts or grants. Once a Continuing Resolution or full-year appropriation is signed into law, the Department will begin implementing the plan to orderly resume activity and will notify contractors/recipients at that time. Thank you for your continued partnership with the Department, and for your cooperation as we work together to manage this lapse in appropriations.

Offerors must rely on the written description provided in the solicitation, including the Government Furnished Property/Equipment inventory at Attachment 2 ("all cooking pots, pans, and kitchen utensils and equipment as per attached"), together with the Performance Work Statement, to assess equipment adequacy for proposal purposes. Solicitation citations: Attachment 2 (Government Furnished Property), page 28; Section 3, Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), page 47. Question 2 � Minimum Staffing Requirements for the MSG Detachment Cook Position (Rephrased from: "Does the Government anticipate service being delivered by a single on-site cook...or is additional support staff...expected or permitted...") The Performance Work Statement identifies the MSG Detachment Cook as the sole Key Personnel position (Section 4.5.1). The Contractor is responsible for furnishing "all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work" under the contract (Section 1.0, Scope of Work). The Government does not mandate a specific staffing structure; Offerors may propose additional support staff (e.g., a kitchen helper) as needed to fully meet the requirements within their firm-fixed monthly price. Solicitation citations: Section 1.0 (Scope of Work), page 8; Section 4.5.1 (Key Personnel � Position and Function), page 11. Question 3 � Anticipated TDY Headcount Beyond the Standing Detachment (Rephrased from: "Beyond the standing detachment of up to eight (8) Marines, what are the typical and maximum numbers of TDY personnel...") Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services) confirms the Contractor shall provide food services for up to eight (8) MSG personnel and shall accommodate additional Temporary Duty (TDY) personnel at no additional cost to the Government. For planning purposes, Offerors should anticipate a not-to-exceed range of up to four (4) additional TDY personnel during surge periods, beyond the standing eight-person detachment. Because this solicitation is for food preparation services only � and not the procurement of ingredients or supplies, which remains a separate Government-managed process under Section 1 (Prices) � any increase in MSG personnel supported during TDY periods, up to this maximum, will not result in additional cost to the Contractor. Offerors should build sufficient flexibility into portioning and menu planning to accommodate periodic increases above the standing detachment. Solicitation citations: Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services), page 9; Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 4 � Existence of a Budgetary Ceiling for Ingredient Purchases (Rephrased from: "As the Government purchases ingredients from the contractor's weekly shopping list, is there a budgetary ceiling, per-person allowance, or historical monthly spend...") The solicitation does not establish a fixed budgetary ceiling or per-person ingredient allowance. Per Section 1 (Prices), the Contractor provides a weekly ingredient shopping list, which the Government (through the Marines) purchases and delivers to the MSGR. This is a Government-managed process separate from the Contractor's firm-fixed monthly price for labor and services. No historical monthly spend figures are being released as part of this solicitation. Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 5 � Confirmation of Set-Aside Status (Rephrased from: "Could you please confirm the set-aside status of this acquisition...") This acquisition is unrestricted. No set-aside applies, per Block 10 of the SF-1449. Solicitation citations: SF-1449, Block 10, page 3. Question 6 � Applicability of the Section 5000C Excise Tax (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C applies to this award, or whether a treaty-based exemption may be claimed...") Per the Zadroga Act notice in Section 1 and Provision 52.229-11 in Section 5, payments under this contract may be subject to the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C unless the Offeror is a U.S. person or qualifies for an exemption. The Netherlands currently maintains an income tax treaty with the United States that may provide a basis for exemption from this excise tax. However, regardless of treaty eligibility, any foreign-person Offeror seeking to claim an exemption must still submit a completed IRS Form W-14 with its quotation. If the form is not submitted, the Government will withhold the full 2% from each payment, per FAR 52.229-11(e)(2). Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Zadroga Act Notice), page 5; Section 5, Provision 52.229-11(e)(2), pages 52�53. Question 7 � Confirmation of Weekday-Only Meal Service (No Weekend Coverage) (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage is expected...") Per PWS �1.2.2 and Attachment 1, meal service is scheduled Monday through Friday, 0700�1800 hours, on a 20-weekday menu cycle. The solicitation does not require any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage. Service is limited strictly to the five weekday service periods described in the meal service schedule. Solicitation citations: PWS �1.2.2, page 8; Attachment 1, page 22. The U.S. Government does not provide guidance, direction, or assistance regarding the nationality classification (e.g., Third Country National, local national, or otherwise) of Contractor personnel. description: W912PM26BA008 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington District requires a contract to perform work of the Eagle Island Cell 2 disposal area. The project includes work at Cell 2 of the Government owned Eagle Island Confined Disposal Facility (CDF) also referred to as the Dredged Material Disposal Area. The work to improve Cell 2 consists of: using existing coffer berms around spillways 4 and 5, as well as the interior of Cell 2 as borrow, raise approximately 2,000 linear feet of the low spots on the west portion of Cell 2 to EL. 46 feet NAVD88 where crest heights range from approximately EL. 37 feet NAVD88 to EL. 45 feet NAVD88 and corresponds with approximate Stations 190+00 to 210+00; raising a few bents of the timber cribbing structures associated with the outfall pipe for spillway 4; repairs to straighten spillways 4 and 5 will consist of deconstructing the riser structures, removing the footing, removing the catwalk, re-grading the bump-out to a 3H:1V slope, prepping the subgrade, pouring a 16-inch footing and reconstructing the riser structure. This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set Aside. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. The Magnitude of Construction of this project is between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 12 August 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $45,000,000.00. It is the Offeror's responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. description: Presolicitation Notice: Synopsis for Commercial Services (Prepared in accordance with RFO Subpart 5.1 and RFO Subpart 12.1) This presolicitation notice is prepared in accordance with the requirements outlined in RFO 5.101, supplemented with additional information provided in this notice. This announcement serves as the public presolicitation notice for this acquisition. A formal written solicitation will not be posted to the System for Award Management (SAM.gov); instead, the Government will solicit quotations directly from suppliers. Solicitation Information Currently, there is no solicitation number for this acquisition. IAW RFO 12.201-1(c)(2) - Simplified Procedures Method To promote maximum competition and streamline acquisition, the Contracting Officer has chosen to solicit quotations directly from suppliers for this acquisition. When soliciting directly, the following conditions apply: A presolicitation notice must be posted in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) per RFO FAR 5.101(a). Quotations must be solicited from a minimum of three sources [RFO 12.201-1(c)(2)(ii)]. Whenever practicable, solicitations should include at least two sources not previously contacted [RFO 12.201-1(c)(2)(iii)]. No formal solicitation document will be posted on SAM.gov. For inquiries, please contact Mr. Cade Zelinsky at cade.s.zelinsky@usace.army.mil or call 816-389-3143. The incorporated provisions and clauses are in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) and the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). (1) Point of Contact [RFO 5.101(c)(1)] Contract Specialist Cade Zelinsky (816) 389-3143 cade.s.zelinsky@usace.army.mil Contracting Officer Christopher W. Anderson (816) 389- 3850 christopher.w.anderson@usace.army.mil (2) Set-aside [RFO 5.101(c)(2) & RFO 6.102-2] Total Small Business Set-Aside (100%) (3) Codes for Services or Supplies [RFO 5.101(c)(3)] a. Product Service Code (PSC): W054 - Lease/Rental of Prefabricated and Portable Buildings b. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS): 531120 - Lessors of Nonresidential Buildings (4) Description of Services and Award Procedures [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(i) & (ii)] The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Kansas City District has a requirement for a lease regarding a 24x60 Office Trailer delivered to the Rathbun Lake Project Office in Centerville, IA. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, and materials required for the requirement. This requirement will be procured using the simplified procedures outlined in RFO 12.201-1. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The anticipated contract award date is 30 October 2026 (5) Technical Data Access [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(iv)] The complete Statement of work (SOW), detailing the specifications, will be provided directly to the solicited vendors. Other interested vendors may request the SOW from the Contract Specialist listed above. (6) Universal Submission Statement [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(vi)] All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. (7) Applicable FAR Clauses [RFO 12.205]: The solicitation and the resulting award incorporate one or more provisions and clauses by reference, carrying the same legal force as if provided in full text. The Contracting Officer will provide full versions upon request. Contractors are advised that certain provisions include data blocks that must be completed and submitted with the quotation. Instead of submitting the full text of these provisions, you may identify them by paragraph identifier and provide the required information. Full text is also available electronically at the following addresses: Federal Acquisition Regulations System (FAR) https://www.acquisition.gov/far Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars **Applicable FAR Clauses: ** - FAR 52.212-1: Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-2: Evaluation - Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-4: Contract Terms and Conditions - Commercial Products and Commercial Services Important SAM Registration Notice: In accordance with FAR provision 52.204-7, incorporated by reference in this solicitation, the prospective awardee must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at https://sam.gov to be eligible for award. Small businesses seeking assistance with registration or navigation can contact the APEX Accelerators (formerly known as PTACs), which is an official government contracting assistance resource for small businesses. Find your local APEX Accelerators to get free help completing registration in SAM.gov. For general inquiries regarding government procurements or assistance in proposal preparation, local APEX Accelerators may be available to help. To locate an APEX near you, visit https://www.napex.us/locations/.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: **** Update as of 08 OCT 2020, the Tech Read Library Instructions have been updated to allow for a digital copy for review by potential Small Business Offerors. Please see below the attached updated instructions to obtain access to the Tech Read Library. The name of the document is C-sUAS Digital Tech Read Library_Instr_20201006. **** **** Update as of 28 AUG 2020, the Government's Acquisition Strategy has been approved and it has been determined that this effort will be solicited as a Small Business set-aside under NAICS 541715 Aircraft, Aircraft Engine and Engine Parts exception with size standard of 1,500 employees. Please continue to watch this posting for updates until the solicitation is released. **** ****Updated 27 AUG 2020, Posted Corrected Version of Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 24 AUG 2020, Posted Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 18 MAR 2020, Due to the COVID-19 spread and site closure the Technical Read Library Access is currently suspended until at least 11 MAY 2020. Please note that depending on the state of things this date can be pushed out further or rescined earlier.**** ****Updated 13 FEB 2020, Posted an Updated version of the Industry Day Attendees List**** ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. The solicitation and any amendments thereto will only be available by downloading the documents from the website. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring the site for the release of amendments (if any) or other information pertaining to the solicitation. It is anticipated that the website will provide a registration service that will send an e-mail notification when a change is made to the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the RFP which shall be considered. Based on market research, the Government is not using FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, to solicit for the described supplies or services. However, interested parties may identify to the Contracting Officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item(s) within thirty (30) days of this notice. Technical questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR), Donna Toole at (315) 330-3972, donna.toole.1@us.af.mil. Any contractual questions or questions concerning this Presolicitation Notice should be communicated directly to the Contract Specialist, Matthew Zawisza at (315) 330-4922, matthew.zawisza@us.af.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil. In accordance with AFFARS 5301.91, an Ombudsman has been appointed to hear and facilitate the resolution of concerns from offerors, potential offerors, and others for this acquisition. Before consulting with an Ombudsman, interested parties must first address their concerns, issues, disagreements, and/or recommendations to the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil, for resolution. AFFARS clause 5352.201-9101, Ombudsman, will be incorporated into the resultant contract. When requested, the Ombudsman will maintain strict confidentiality as to the source of the concern. The existence of the Ombudsman does not affect the authority of the Program Manager, Contracting Officer, or source selection official. Further, the Ombudsman does not participate in the evaluation of proposals, the source selection process, or the adjudication of protests or formal contract disputes. The Ombudsman may refer the party to another official who can resolve the concern. Consulting an Ombudsman does not alter or postpone the timelines for any other processes (e.g., agency level bid protests, GAO bid protests, requests for debriefings, employee-employer actions, contests of OMB Circular A-76 competition performance decisions). If resolution cannot be made by the Contracting Officer, concerned parties may contact the following AFRL Ombudsman: Mr. Steven L. Ewers, 1864 Fourth Street, Wright-Patterson AFB OH 45433-7130, COMM (937) 904-4407, email: steven.ewers@us.af.mil. Concerns, issues, disagreements, and recommendations that cannot be resolved at the AFRL level may be brought by the concerned party for further consideration to the Air Force Ombudsman, Associate Deputy
